'I knew everything about the universe / about them / about human evolution' is the experiencer becoming omniscient, the exact inverse of being known (6 passages); 'Nothing was hidden' meaning panoramic 360-degree vision or cosmic transparency, not personal exposure ('there was nothing hidden from me. So while I'm looking to the left, I'm still seeing to the right'); Scripture quotation (Luke 8:17, nothing hidden that will not be revealed); Speculation about a future heavenly reunion where 'there's nothing to hide'; Ordinary life: a wife who 'knew me better than probably anyone else'; Acceptance or mutual recognition without the knowing (a grandmother who 'knew me very well too').

places.name: the preview
places.description: The forward-facing twin of the review. Instead of, or alongside, what you did, you are shown what is coming - your own future, your children growing up, the life your family will have with or without you, or events on a global scale. Experiencers are careful to distinguish two grades: things that will definitely occur and things that are only possible, since free will has not been spent. The corpus's own term for it is 'life preview'. Several are shown their family's life if they do not return, and this is what decides them.
sensory: shown on the same screen or in the same field as the past
graded into 'definite' and 'possible but not definite'
personal futures (a child's bedroom, a funeral, a graduation) far more common than global ones
sometimes explicitly withdrawn afterwards: 'I'm not allowed to know the future'

quotes.text: Then they showed me through the same screen some future events in my life if I chose to return to it. Some events would definitely occur, and some events were possible but not definite.
quotes.speaker: Karen Thomas

quotes.text: So there's no life review. But in my case, there's a life preview. And at the time, I didn't realize how far it went.
Then I was shown the future without me.

places.notes: One of the strongest cvNDE gradients in the region: 3.74% of all accounts but 7.73% of the best-evidenced ones. This is intuitive - a shown future is checkable, so accounts containing one are more likely to score highly on veridical evidence. Precision loss comes from interviewer questions about 'the future of humanity' and from channelled future-prediction segments unconnected to the NDE itself. Audit found false positives of the form: Podcast and radio boilerplate — host intros, 'link in the description', episode teasers that list 'visions of possible future events' (four passages); A YouTube narrator analysing somebody ELSE's NDE and its predictions; A researcher's statistical aside: 'of the 1200 testimonies I've heard, a very small percentage are shown future events'; Precognitive dreams in ordinary life and future-seeing in a past-life regression — not the NDE; 'our perception of future events' used in a general talk about which emotions survive death.

places.name: Light Everywhere, With No Source and No Shadow
places.description: A quieter and more distinctive observation than the bright-light encounter: once inside, experiencers notice there is no sun and no shadow. They check under leaves, behind rocks, beneath their own feet, and find nothing dark. The explanation offered inside the experience is usually that the light comes from within every object rather than falling on it — 'everything was made of light'. This is the corpus's most physically specific claim about the light.

aliases.term: light coming from within every object
no sun, no moon, yet there's a light from everywhere
the light of God which shines on everything

aliases.note: 'this life is black and white. Heaven is living color.'

sensory: leaves, rocks and plants inspected specifically for shadows and found to have none
depth without darkness — 'there's depth to things without having darkness'
objects lit from the inside; the grass, the trees and the body all made of light
one painter's frustration: you cannot paint it, because painting brightness requires dark contrast
colours become impossible to render — 'millions of blues, millions of greens'

quotes.text: There was light everywhere but no sun. The light seemed to come from within everything, even the air.
quotes.speaker: Anthony

quotes.text: There were just no shadows. Jesus had no shadow. I had no shadow.
quotes.speaker: Debbie Ali

quotes.text: I realized that everything was lit up, yet there was no sun. There's no shadows, there's no moon, yet there's a light from everywhere.
quotes.speaker: Kenneth McDonald

quotes.text: everything was made of light even though there were individual things and beings
quotes.speaker: Lisa M

places.notes: Flat across strata (5.65% all, 5.66% at cv>=18, 4.97% at cv>=23). Note that several of the 'no shadows' documents are the same speaker (Debbie Ali) retold across different channels, so document count overstates the number of distinct witnesses for that phrasing. Audit found false positives of the form: 'Made of light' describing BEINGS — angels, God, an alien, robed figures, orbs — not the shadowless environment. Nine passages, and it is a different (already well-attested) feature of the corpus; Theological inference ('God is light, we're made in his image, so we're made of light'); Interviewer reading the experiencer's own book back to them; 'We're made of light and energy' asserted from a hospital bed as general metaphysics; One pure idiom: 'for me I had no shadow' in a story about a job selection process.

places.name: Being Absorbed Into the Light
places.description: Rather than arriving at the light, some are taken into it and stop being separate from it. The recurring images are dissolution without loss: sugar stirred into water, a drop returning to the ocean, melting, being taken apart molecule by molecule and put back together. A minority report fear at this point — fear of losing their individuality — and several say they remained themselves and one with it simultaneously.

aliases.note: 'one billionth of a drop of water in the ocean being reunited'

sensory: loss of body boundary while retaining awareness of self
sugar-into-water and drop-into-ocean similes recur independently
'taken apart molecule by molecule and put back together'
sometimes a chorus of other lights saying 'welcome home' just before absorption
one recurring fear: 'I started to be afraid of losing myself in the light'

quotes.text: I plunged, plunged into it and merged, and merged with this light. At which point, everything changed. My personal sense of identity was gone at that point. I was this light.
quotes.speaker: Dr. Karl Simanonok

quotes.text: I didn't go into the light. I was absorbed into the light.
quotes.speaker: Andy Petro

quotes.text: I became one with the light, and the more I became one with the light, the better I felt.
quotes.speaker: Lee Whitting

quotes.text: Like I just melted into the light. So comforting.
quotes.speaker: Drew Brophy

places.notes: SLIGHTLY LESS common among better-evidenced accounts (3.81% all vs 3.45% at cv>=18, 3.31% at cv>=23) — consistent with the structured report, where cosmic_unity also falls from 60.9% to 49.2% as evidential strength rises. Precision is the weakest of my set: roughly a third of matches are retrospective philosophising ('we're already merged with Source') rather than a described moment in the experience. Audit found false positives of the form: Theological debate about whether one is OBLIGED to dissolve back into Source — free-will commentary, hypothetical and future-tense ('if you want to merge with source, you can'), two passages from the same speaker; The interviewer's own question ('can you focus on the mechanics of the merger?') and a host reading from the guest's book; Observing OTHER souls already merged with God rather than being absorbed oneself (two passages); Meditation/stillness talk about 'becoming one with everything', and a YouTube-channel plug about 'the whole idea of enlightenment and merging with God'.

places.name: the children who pull you back
places.description: The single commonest reason people choose to come back. Not love of life, not fear of death, not unfinished ambition — a child. Experiencers who are otherwise entirely unwilling to return describe the thought of a son, daughter or baby arriving and the decision being made instantly and irreversibly. Several report knowing exactly what would happen to those children if they stayed, and that this is what settles it.

aliases.term: I need to be there for them

sensory: the children's faces appearing in front of the experiencer, looking back at them
the decision described as forming before the question has finished
'the hardest decision I had ever had to make'
the offer to stay withdrawing itself the instant the thought lands

quotes.text: I wanted to go back for my children. I knew deep down they needed me and nothing was going to stop me from getting back to them.
quotes.speaker: Tara

quotes.text: And I remember going, "My daughter needs me. I need to get back."
quotes.speaker: Laura D

quotes.text: I also saw that I couldn't leave my children to stay in this carefree place.
I felt I could stay there, then glanced around at my Son, my Wife, and finally, my baby girl, and something told me I need to be there for them.
quotes.speaker: Lorraine

quotes.text: And I knew that my kids needed me

places.notes: Rises with evidential strength (3.89% -> 5.52%). One experiencer (RROedrc0Nw8) turns this into practical advice for paramedics: that saying 'your children need you' to a coding patient may reach them where their own name does not. Precision limited by medical narrative uses of 'my son needs an operation'. Audit found false positives of the form: Ordinary parenting and biography: custody battles, a child born with Down syndrome, 'my children really needed somebody to help take care of them' while she was ill; 'my kids need me' shouted in the hospital room to get a doctor's attention — the medical setting, not the other side; Two near-duplicate OBE passages where 'my kids need me' only explains why she habitually checks the clock; Advice to paramedics that they should say 'your children need you' at a resuscitation — speculation about others; Channel boilerplate (Instagram/website sign-off) that happens to mention 'my kids'.

places.name: Where We Came From
places.description: Beyond familiarity, a stronger claim: this is the place of origin, and the earthly life was the departure from it. Experiencers describe arriving back at a starting point rather than reaching a destination. It is often told as a discovery made in the moment — 'I know that this is where I came from' — and is frequently what converts the experience from an event into a cosmology.

aliases.term: I knew you before you were ever born
aliases.note: scriptural framing offered by Christian experiencers

sensory: described as a 'larger matrix' one has been separated from
the sense of arriving at a source rather than a destination
often paired with the immediate refusal to leave again

quotes.text: Then, with a sudden burst of joy, I realized that this was my real home. Back on Earth, I had been a visitor, a misfit, and a homesick stranger.
quotes.speaker: Arthur

quotes.text: This is where we came from. This is where we're going to return to. And this is really all that matters.
quotes.speaker: Deborah King

quotes.text: I really felt like I was going home. This is where I came from.
quotes.speaker: Mary Jo Rapini

quotes.text: I got to the actual place we would consider heaven or home where we all came from.
that place is what I believe to be my real home. And this is not all that there is.
quotes.speaker: Bubba Herrick

places.notes: Flat across strata (3.93% / 3.87% / 4.42%) — neither strengthened nor weakened by evidential quality. Overlaps the-home heavily by design; kept separate because the claim is different in kind. Home is a felt quality; 'where I came from' is a cosmological assertion about origin, and it is the hinge on which many accounts turn toward pre-birth existence and reincarnation language. False positives are biographical ('the church I came from') and are handled by the negative regex. Audit found false positives of the form: The exact inversion: 'they were going to send me back to where I came from' / 'I turned around to go back where I came from' — here 'where I came from' means Earth or a direction in space, not the origin; Post-hoc sermon and affirmation material ('our true home is in the spiritual world', 'that's where we came from, we came here with free will') — general cosmology, not a perception; A poem read aloud from a book about returning 'to where we all come from'; Untranslatable philosophical rambling where 'we came from there' is a rhetorical aside.

places.name: the veil of forgetting
places.description: The threshold on the way back, where what was known is taken away again. Experiencers report being told they will not be allowed to keep it, or discovering afterwards that specifically the answers - and only the answers - have been erased. Several say the knowledge is still in them but sealed; a few say fragments surface over decades. The withdrawal is usually described as deliberate and purposeful rather than as ordinary forgetting, and it is often explained to them: remembering would remove the point of being here.

aliases.term: a helmet of lead collapsed over my consciousness
aliases.note: one experiencer's image for the moment of return

sensory: a lead helmet closing over the mind at the instant of return
the answers specifically removed while the events remain
memories surfacing gradually over years afterwards
knowing that you knew, without being able to reach it

quotes.text: I knew all things. I knew everything. I even had the reason for the earth years, why we had to do time on Earth. I knew that over there, but I couldn't bring it back with me.
quotes.speaker: Mark

quotes.text: these answers were erased. That's the the only thing that was erased through this whole event were the answers to the questions that we all have.
quotes.speaker: Ana Christina

quotes.text: Most of the knowledge that I gained in that expanded state, I was not allowed to remember.
quotes.speaker: Melissa Denyce

quotes.text: We had to go through a veil of forgetfulness because that love is so strong and so powerful that even the remembrance of that love would prevent us from having true free agency.
quotes.speaker: Vinnie Todd Tolman

places.notes: An earlier, looser version of this regex reached 10.75% but was dominated by 'I can't take it anymore' from the dying-body narrative; this tightened version trades recall for precision. Some hits are the mirror-image doctrine (a pre-birth veil placed before incarnation) rather than the post-NDE withdrawal - the corpus itself treats these as the same mechanism running in two directions. Audit found false positives of the form: The inverted case: being told 'you WILL remember this' as a charge to carry a message or a prophecy back (a dying friend's message to his wife, a Hajj prediction, a week-ahead job prophecy) — the regex cannot tell being made to remember from being made to forget; Ordinary forgetting in biography ('I don't remember him there' at an accident scene); General commentary about NDErs 'taking off the veil of forgetfulness', framed through a Peter Pan analogy rather than a personal report; One restriction on perception rather than memory ('there are some things you can't see or are not allowed to know' about the being's appearance).

places.name: How the dead appear: restored
places.description: Uniformly, the dead are not as they died. Amputations, cancer, dementia, wheelchairs and old age are gone. The most commonly cited apparent age is the mid-twenties to mid-thirties regardless of the age at death, and several experiencers were unable to recognise a parent for that reason until afterwards. A recurring refinement: the being first appears at the age you would recognise, then visibly changes to its restored age once recognition has happened.

aliases.term: in the prime of their life

sensory: mid-twenties to mid-thirties is the modal apparent age
eyes 'more light than eyes'
no wrinkles, no weight, no heaviness, no pain
period-appropriate clothing but a restored body inside it
the being may deliberately appear old first so you can identify them, then shift younger

quotes.text: My father was also standing. I had never in my life seen him stand or walk. He looked vibrant and in the prime of his life, and I was ecstatic. He was healed.
the reason I didn't recognize him was because he was younger. He looked like my husband's age. He looked about 30 years old.
quotes.speaker: Kim Carrey

quotes.text: He appeared as an old man so he could be easily recognized, then changed to look younger, about thirty.
quotes.speaker: John Hernandez

quotes.text: I saw thousands of people there, including my mom, grandmothers, and aunt, and an uncle. Everyone looked 25 to 30 years old.

places.notes: Clearly enriched in better-evidenced accounts (3.79% -> 5.66%). This regex is the third draft; the first two were swamped by 'when I was younger', which is why that phrase is in the negative_regex. Residual false positives are mostly the experiencer describing their OWN restored body rather than a greeter's, which is arguably the same phenomenon. Audit found false positives of the form: Recurring junk: the experiencer's OWN restored/young spirit body ('I looked 25 at 40', 'my hands looked like I was 18', looking younger in the mirror afterwards) — 4 passages. That is a real feature but a different one; it should not be counted as 'how the dead appear'; Descriptions of Jesus's appearance (healthy, in his prime, not battered) and of an unidentified old-bearded being with young skin — beings, not deceased loved ones; Pure biography (a dinner shift with stomach pain) and post-NDE self-talk about 'the Alyssa that was no longer sick'; Channel commentary generalising that 'loved ones look like they're in the prime of their life' rather than a firsthand sighting; One passage framed explicitly as a dream in a hospital room.

places.name: The Vortex — the Passage That Spins
places.description: A distinct minority variant of the passage: it does not merely carry you, it turns you. People describe corkscrewing forward, a spinning or circular motion, a whirlpool, a tornado with walls twisting around themselves, or being thrown into a vortex so violent they had to hold on to the walls. Where the plain tunnel is often peaceful, the turning passage is more often frightening or at least strenuous, and it appears at both the outbound and the return end of the journey.

aliases.note: 'a rainbow-colored whirlpool, but it was upside down'
'the interior of a pitch-black tornado with the walls twisting around themselves endlessly'
the corpus's own spelling in one account

sensory: forward rotation, not just spin — 'a forward rotation that was happening like a corkcrew'
walls twisting around themselves endlessly
streaks of blue light on the sides that can be heard as well as seen
having to grip the walls to avoid being flung out
an upside-down whirlpool that goes up rather than down
counterclockwise circling of light-beings around the traveller

quotes.text: the tunnel sort of twisted and it corkscrewed. So there was movement. It wasn't just static like turning around me. It was turning and moving at the same time
It's this dark, kind of dark tunnel. It has some lights in it. It's a vortex. So it's moving in a circular motion.
quotes.speaker: Sharon Milliman

quotes.text: there was this sort of movement like a corkscrew of circular circling forward through this tunnel
quotes.speaker: Peter Bard

quotes.text: the tunnel was corkcrewing, right? It wasn't just spinning like this. It was moving forward.
quotes.speaker: David Ditchfield

quotes.text: And I was thrown into this vortex, as all I can describe it as.
quotes.speaker: Andrea Courey

places.notes: Slightly more common at cv>=13/18 (5.01%/5.11% vs 4.19% all) but LESS common at cv>=23 (3.87%) — with only 7 hits at that stratum the difference is not meaningful. The main precision leak is New Age geographic 'vortexes' (Sedona, Mount Shasta, Hawaii) and metaphorical downward spirals, which the negative_regex targets. Worth keeping separate from the plain tunnel because the rotation is consistently volunteered as the surprising, un-clichéd detail: 'not everybody does the tunnel, but I did the tunnel... I felt like I was corkscrewing'. Audit found false positives of the form: The hospital whirlpool bath in the physiotherapy department (two near-duplicate passages) — a literal medical whirlpool, not a passage; Life-story metaphor: 'I kept spiraling further downhill', 'my health spiraled down very fast'; 'vortex of the child welfare system' — pure figure of speech from an unrelated narrative; Swirling things that are not passages: colours swirled through God's throne, a whirling mist visitation, a swirling hourglass of light seen at a distance; Swirl at the moment of exit in a meditation-induced OBE, not an NDE transit.

places.name: The crowd
places.description: Beyond the named greeters there is very often a mass — dozens, hundreds, thousands, 'a huge group of people, dozens and dozens and dozens', a kingdom 'populated by tremendous numbers of people'. The crowd is busy: working, learning, involved with the living. Experiencers report loving all of them and knowing all of them individually, which is one of the most reliably strange claims in the corpus.

aliases.term: the whole crowd extended far into the distance

sensory: extends back into shadow — you know who each shadow is anyway
people from visibly different time periods, in period dress
no one old, no one sick, no one crying
they are working and learning, not idle
in some accounts they are past lives of the experiencer, not other people

quotes.text: On the other side of the river were hundreds of souls, and I knew that during many lifetimes I had lived and interacted with them.
quotes.speaker: Norma Edwards

quotes.text: there was a huge group of people, dozens and dozens and dozens, maybe even hundreds.
quotes.speaker: Amber Cavanagh

quotes.text: And I could see that there were many people, as populated by tremendous numbers of people. And I knew each and every one of them intimately.
quotes.speaker: Reinee Pasarow

places.notes: Nearly doubles from all accounts to the best-evidenced (3.74% -> 7.18%). An earlier unconstrained version ('group of people') matched 924 docs at ~30% precision — almost all ordinary biography — so the context clause is load-bearing. 'Soul family / soul group' alone matches 283 docs (4.58%) but is a New Age framing that runs the OTHER way across strata (5.26% all vs 2.76% cv>=23), so I kept it out of the measured regex and listed it only as an alias. Audit found false positives of the form: 'group of souls' used for reincarnation soul-group philosophy ('the same thousand or 10,000 will come back into your life in lifetimes') rather than a perceived crowd; Small councils of three, four or twelve beings — structurally the opposite of the mass the claim describes; A channelled entity ('still heirlam speaking') lecturing about what happens when 'a group of souls' works with dark intention; A psychic telling the guest he is 'protected by thousands of angels right now', plus a book plug; Two duplicate passages where the group is eight shadowed figures in a hospital hallway; New-age oversoul/fractal theorising where 'group of beings' means humanity.

places.name: the screen
places.description: The most common physical staging of the review: a screen, or many screens, on which your life plays. People reach for cinema again and again - a movie theatre, a curtain that parts, a countdown, an old black-and-white reel, a vintage projector clicking in one ear. Several describe a round room ringed with fifteen or twenty screens, each running a different age of your life at once. Some are careful to say the screen was a frame of reference their mind supplied, not the thing itself.

aliases.note: 'God and I were in a big movie theater in the galaxy'
often explicitly old-fashioned, black-and-white, 35mm
several hear the projector sound before seeing anything
one experiencer's idiosyncratic frame of reference for the same function

sensory: black-and-white, old-fashioned, silent
a curtain of stars parting to the right
the clicking sound of a vintage projector, heard in one ear
fifteen to twenty screens ringing a round room, one per age
a title card with your own name on it

quotes.text: instead of having the screen in the front, the movie screens were all on the top in a big circle. There must have been maybe 15 or, or 20 of these screens.
quotes.speaker: John Davis

quotes.text: And it revealed a larger-than-life movie screen. And I heard the countdown of the numbers, three, two, one. And I saw the title in front of me, "The Life Review of Erica McKenzie."
quotes.speaker: Erica McKenzie

quotes.text: It was like a round theater and on top of me or on and the on the ceiling were all these movie screens and there must have been like 15 or 20 of these and they were all in a circle.
quotes.speaker: John J Davis

quotes.text: the screen comes down and I'm watching this screen and it was like watching an oldfashioned black and white movie on an oldfashioned movie reel.
quotes.speaker: Sharon Milliman

places.notes: The cinema staging is culturally loaded and several experiencers push back on it explicitly - 'it wasn't like watching a movie screen or anything as simple as that', 'instead of just watching it like you'd watch a movie or a film strip, I became myself again'. The screen and the surround (see the-surround) are therefore best read as two competing accounts of the same event: spectator versus participant. Remaining false positives are host chatter about what is 'on the screen' of the video. Audit found false positives of the form: Passages that mention 'life review' with no screen, movie or projector at all — the regex appears to match the review itself rather than its staging; Explicit denials of the cinema frame: 'it's often described as a film, but for me it wasn't a film, it was all the information at once'; Generalised teaching about what everyone does after death ('you go with your team of guides and you watch the movie of your life'); Pop-culture jokes ('like that movie Defending Your Life', 'a Netflix documentary about your life'); 'Movies/films' as ordinary-life content inside the review — school Duck-and-Cover films, 'teachers, schools, movies, media'; A film reel of the whole earth's history that the experiencer explicitly says was NOT a life review.

places.name: The Source / The Creator / The Universe
places.description: The name reached for by experiencers who find 'God' too small, too human or too religious. The Source is described as where everything comes from and returns to — 'the source of all creation', 'the source of all being', 'the womb of God'. Many use it interchangeably with God and say so explicitly, stacking the names together: 'source, God, all the words are far too small'. Others prefer 'the Creator', 'the Universe', 'all that is', or 'universal consciousness'.

aliases.note: used by one prominent account for a deity 'too big' for the word God
used of the 'blacklight' variant of the Source

sensory: described as a centre — 'the center of everything', with everything else radiating from it
sometimes seen as a vast cluster of uncountable suns
occasionally reported as dark rather than bright — the 'blacklight', 'an endless void of pitch blackness bursting with healing power'
pulses, and each pulse sends out individual souls

quotes.text: I just knew straight away that this was the source of all creation that I was looking at. This was God, you know, this was, this is where it all comes from.
quotes.speaker: Dody

quotes.text: I didn't see God because the light that I was in was God. The light was the creator. The light is everything.
quotes.speaker: Philip Siracusa

quotes.text: I was being told that what I was looking at here was the source of all creation
quotes.speaker: David Ditchfield

quotes.text: Everything that is comes from the light. It's the source of all being.
quotes.speaker: Derick McDaniel

quotes.text: i knew i was in the presence of divine love, god, source energy.

places.notes: LESS common among better-evidenced accounts — 7.59% all, 6.08% at cv>=18, 4.97% at cv>=23. Lowest precision in my set: about 40% of matches are the speaker's present-day vocabulary rather than a described encounter, because 'source' has become house style in parts of the NDE-interview world. The cleanest sub-signal is 'the source of all creation/being', which is almost always a description of what was seen. Audit found false positives of the form: 'Source' overwhelmingly appears as a name-stack in general spiritual teaching rather than as something perceived — 'God, Source, the universe, whatever name you want to plug in', 'we all come from the same source', 'we are made of source energy' (P5, P7, P11, P12, P13, P14, P17, P20, P22).; Interviewer clarifications and host boilerplate that recite the name list ('some people could call it God, people could call it Source'; 'she reports source god provided her with...') (P15, P23).; New-age commentary unconnected to any experience — scalar/portal theory, channelled explanations of how manifestation works, God-as-learner metaphysics (P10, P16, P22).; Someone else's NDE summarised by a narrator ('she felt cradled in the heart of the source of all love') (P9).; Post-experience after-effects rather than the experience ('experiencing my oneness with the source 24/7 while driving my car') (P2), and a passage where 'Source God' is only an aside while the place described is hell (P3)..

places.name: The weight of the body
places.description: The immediate aftermath of return: pain floods back, and the body is experienced as intolerably heavy, dense, small, dull and slow after weightlessness. The recurring similes are clothing and confinement — a heavy wet diving suit, wet clothes, clay, a glove, a tent, a prison. Several experiencers say the grief and guilt they had been free of returns in the same instant as the physical pain.

aliases.term: it was so heavy to be back in the body
like donning a heavy, tight diving suit
a little pup tent or prison
I felt like I was wearing my body

sensory: gravity felt as a novel sensation, in the joints
the body as wet, heavy clothing you must put back on
slow, dull, dense — 'the physical here, it seems dead'
emotional pain returns simultaneously with physical pain
a small number report no pain at all: 'I popped back into my body, and it didn't hurt'

quotes.text: But back to the grief and the pain and the regret and the guilt and the trauma. It was so heavy to be back in the body.
quotes.speaker: Jeffrey Olsen

quotes.text: When she finally put me back into my body, the transition felt like donning a heavy, tight diving suit.
quotes.speaker: Brian

quotes.text: So I snapped back into my body and coming back to my form was excruciatingly painful.
quotes.speaker: Daniel Giroux

quotes.text: it brought me back into my body and it was just I have to say it was just horrible because I felt from this expanded state of consciousness back into this constricted
quotes.speaker: Tammy Lee Anderson

places.notes: Doubles across the strata (1.60% -> 3.31%), monotone. Very high precision. This is the quietest and least-discussed part of the arc, but it is the emotional inverse of the peace that opens the experience, and experiencers reach for the same small set of clothing metaphors independently of one another, which is worth flagging to whoever builds the alias graph. Audit found false positives of the form: An interviewer stating the claim on behalf of other experiencers — 'Some near-death experiencers say that it was painful to come back into the body because they felt very constrained' — and the guest rejecting it: 'I was so happy to be back' (VfxlSpSuxuI).; One passage where the pain on return is the ongoing grief of having lost a child, i.e. life circumstance rather than the weight of re-entry (XUBmfoItQ7M).; Otherwise unusually clean; the similes the claim predicts all show up verbatim (diving suit, prison, bottle, toothpaste tube, clay). Two of the strongest passages are the same account transcribed twice (KQNAmYgHmEQ, Xna-HGgLytk)..

places.name: The grey place / the in-between
places.description: Neither light nor dark: a colourless, foggy, half-lit country populated by people who seem stuck. Experiencers describe wandering figures who do not look up, do not speak, and appear unaware they can leave. The distress here is not pain but drabness and pointlessness — this life with the life drained out of it. Different traditions supply different names for the same terrain.

aliases.note: Ryan Cook coined it himself: 'this life void of life'
described as 'the cleansing station'
'the wandering souls who never did anything to help anybody... they just wander around suffering'
'where like ghosts and spirits and lost souls hang out'

sensory: colour drains out the further you walk
fog, mist, a dusty ramshackle quality
filthy or grey-white clothing on the inhabitants
faces turned down; no one makes eye contact
silence, or a low murmur rather than screaming

quotes.text: They seemed to be stuck and very much in sorrow. Was this Purgatory? I do not know.
quotes.speaker: Moren

quotes.text: I nicknamed it the gray world, because that's exactly all you see.
quotes.speaker: Ryan Cook

quotes.text: So I think I made it over there to the lower astral realm, you know, where like ghosts and spirits and lost souls hang out.
quotes.speaker: Rich Lopp

quotes.text: it's filled with people. And they're all in these filthy white robes.
quotes.speaker: Angie Fenimore

quotes.text: But what I do know is that it was somewhere where I wouldn't want to be ending up again.
quotes.speaker: Raymond O'Brien

places.notes: LESS common among the best-evidenced accounts (6.01% overall, 3.31% at cv>=23), the sharpest negative gradient in this region. That is partly a genuine signal and partly an artifact: 'purgatory' and 'limbo' are often invoked as theological vocabulary in reflective discussion rather than as descriptions of somewhere visited, and reflective discussion is not what raises a cvNDE score. Precision ~0.5 for that reason. The distinctive and defensible core — a grey, colourless country with people stuck in it who do not seem to know they are stuck — is reported independently by Christian, Catholic, Buddhist and secular experiencers using their own tradition's name for it, which is the strongest synonymy finding in my region. Audit found false positives of the form: 'Purgatory' as Catholic doctrine rather than perceived terrain: childhood catechism, Medjugorje visionaries, indulgence arithmetic, 'there's nobody floating around in purgatory'; 'Purgatory' as a theory about other souls — mediums describing clients, Monroe Institute speculation that belief systems can strand people; Earth itself called purgatory ('this is purgatory, and we've already lived it'); 'Lost souls' as astral-plane instruction addressed to the listener in the second person; Documentary voiceover narrating a third party's hellish NDE; Content recovered in a hypnosis session rather than during the NDE.

places.name: the hall of records
places.description: A building where everything that has happened is kept. Descriptions converge on institutional architecture - marble columns, a triangular pediment, wide steps, 'like the Supreme Court building', 'like the Lincoln Memorial' - and inside, a library of impossible size with twenty-foot shelves and people quietly reading and studying. Others encounter it not as a building but as a field of information you can simply attend to. Names vary by tradition: the Akashic Records, the Hall of Records, the hall of knowledge, the Book of Life, the Great Book of Judgment.

aliases.note: a round room with aisles leading in from all sides and the stars visible overhead
a registration book in which arrivals are recorded

aliases.term: I am the book of life
aliases.note: one experiencer rejects the external record entirely: the record IS the person
often described as a building, not an abstraction: 'a big building up in heaven'
one speaker coins it herself and says she isn't sure that's its real name
one speaker's own name for the same thing, described as a crystallized theatre
with long corridors of books and scrolls radiating out
merged duplicate

sensory: marble columns, triangular pediment, long flights of steps
brown wooden bookshelves twenty feet high, full of books everywhere
gold, chandeliers, a big magnificent room
a round room with aisles from every side and the stars visible above
other people already there, reading, studying, visiting
bookshelves going up further than you can see - no visible ceiling
marble and dark wood, ladders you can slide along to reach high shelves
scrolls: some rolled, some cloth, some rasping paper, some etched flat

quotes.text: My guide communicated to me, this is where the books of life are stored, but we are going to another area.
quotes.speaker: Karen Thomas

quotes.text: after you go through your life review, and you know, you go through the Hall of Records, the Akashic Records, whatever you call it
quotes.speaker: Bill Tortorella

quotes.text: I think I was in the Hall of Records. Now that I've learned, you know, what, how it's been, others have described it.
quotes.speaker: Randy Schiefer

quotes.text: The hall of knowledge is a wonderful place, where one can listen to spiritual teachers.
quotes.speaker: Bettina-Suvi Rode

quotes.text: The call of Records or the Great Book of Judgment and all those terms that we hear, something like that does exist.
quotes.speaker: Dannion Brinkley

places.notes: Strongly enriched in the best-evidenced stratum (5.55% all vs 9.39% at cv>=23). Precision is the weakest of the well-attested places here: 'akashic records' is frequently discussed as a concept rather than a visited place, and 'book of life' sometimes appears in doctrinal argument. Kept because the architectural descriptions, when they do occur, are unusually concrete and mutually consistent. Audit found false positives of the form: 'Lamb's Book of Life' as scripture, preaching and closing prayer — pure doctrine, never a perceived place (4 passages); 'Akashic Records' as a present-day practice: dice divination, paid readings, psychic sessions, 'I know a couple that work with the Akashic Records'; Generalising about what OTHER NDErs report ('other people who have NDEs sometimes speak of going to a Hall of Records'); Metaphor ('we're different chapters in one book of life') and denial of the building ('I am the freaking Book of Life'); An earthly library in an unrelated vision about a priest's book collection.

places.name: The Living Grass
places.description: The single most distinctive thing in this region: grass that is awake. Experiencers report that each individual blade has its own consciousness, its own shade of green, and its own light; that the grass knows they are there and is glad; that it parts to accept the foot and closes back around the ankle; that light ripples out through it where they step. Several say they could have stayed looking at the grass for a hundred years.

aliases.note: the canonical phrasing

aliases.term: grass that sings / sings the praises of God

aliases.note: energy/consciousness idiom

sensory: millions or billions of distinguishable shades of green
light emitted from inside each blade; ripples of light under the feet
soft underfoot; does not hurt or resist; parts and closes around the foot
a sweet smell and even a taste when touched
audible — a hum, a note, a symphony, singing
love or energy felt flowing up through the soles of the feet

quotes.text: each blade of grass had its own distinguishing shade of green. So that means there's billions and billions of shades of green.
quotes.speaker: Vinney Tolman

quotes.text: And I could see the grass, every blade of grass moving independently. And it was alive and it was happy to see me.
quotes.speaker: Jason Janas

quotes.text: And each blade of grass had a consciousness in it. Every single blade had a consciousness.
quotes.speaker: Vincent Todd Tolman

quotes.text: the grass wrapped back around my foot and my ankle and it was caressing me
quotes.speaker: Juliann

quotes.text: I could see each blade and each blade was singing. Each blade of grass was singing the praises of God.
quotes.speaker: Heidi Barr

places.notes: This is the strongest cvNDE gradient in the whole region: 1.75% of all accounts but 7.73% of accounts scoring cv>=23 — four and a half times enriched among the best-evidenced. That pattern is worth flagging: the more evidentially solid the account, the more likely the grass is described as conscious. False positives are metaphorical or theological uses ('He knew the number of every blade of grass on Earth', 'I couldn't create one blade of grass') and post-NDE aftereffect passages about earthly lawns. Note that several of the richest testimonies (Vinney/Vincent Tolman) recur under multiple videoIds, so document counts slightly overstate the number of distinct experiencers. Audit found false positives of the form: Only one non-testimony passage: the host reading a quotation from the guest's book and name-dropping another guest's grass story (swpIEufGRUQ). The described phenomenon is genuine but the speaker is the interviewer, so it fails the strict test.; Everything else was first-person and on target — this is the cleanest packet in my batch. Several near-duplicate transcripts of the same accounts (mUzS5gHTAvI/J7u2nHmclrs, f5dO4hsR8_M/SV712eZNI3o, IZWbojibwyA/hhADKDdhTTk) inflate the apparent independence of the evidence and should be de-duplicated before counting accounts..

places.name: The Silence
places.description: The other extreme of the same axis: an absolute quiet with no sound at all, arriving the instant the body's noise (heartbeat, breathing, sirens, the code team) stops. Experiencers stress that no earthly place is ever truly silent, and describe craving that silence for the rest of their lives. Several report it coexisting with music without contradiction.

aliases.note: one experiencer's coinage, repeated across her interviews

sensory: the heartbeat/drumming in the ears cuts out first
silence that is full rather than empty
coexists with the music - both reported at once
afterwards the person hides in closets and chapels trying to find it again

quotes.text: I was instantly impressed by the complete silence. You know, having gone from this chaotic hospital room with so many noises.
quotes.speaker: Brian Hoyland

quotes.text: Not there! It was perfect silence.
quotes.speaker: Tony Woody

quotes.text: And it's what I call the silence behind the silence.
quotes.speaker: Ingrid Honkala

quotes.text: there was absolute silence and that there was a beautiful tune no human being could write
quotes.speaker: Josef Johann Atzmüller

quotes.text: All the noise was gone, and I experienced this profound, profound silence.
quotes.speaker: Ingrid Honkala

places.notes: Strongly MORE common in the best-evidenced accounts - 2.30% overall but 5.52% at cvNDE>=23, a 2.4x enrichment. Nobody catalogued it because the themed briefs were all about sound as event (the rushing sound, the music); the silence is its opposite and equally reported. A few false positives are the 'family silence' about abuse. Audit found false positives of the form: 'Dead silence' in ordinary conversation — a pause on a phone call with a mother, an audience going quiet after a talk; 'Absolute stillness' used for emotional calm rather than absence of sound (a pool of peace dissolving shame) — the same account appears twice in the sample, once quoted, so it costs two of the six errors; Grief silence in an empty house after the children have gone ('the silence just absolutely screams'); Stillness meaning immobility — hiding motionless as a small lizard creature while something hunts it.

places.name: The Animals of the Country
places.description: The landscape is inhabited. Dogs, cats, horses, birds and butterflies are seen playing in the meadow, often including the experiencer's own dead pets, restored to health and youth. Predators and prey are at peace with each other. Several people report the animals communicating telepathically, and a few describe creatures with no earthly counterpart — birds with three separated tails, huge animals flying in the sky.

aliases.note: central to Eben Alexander's account

aliases.term: a swan that spoke by telepathy
aliases.note: rare but vivid single report

sensory: animals young, healthy and free of sickness
no fear between species; no predation
telepathic communication rather than sound
birds and butterflies in colours not seen on earth
pets waiting specifically for their person

quotes.text: There were no people there. There were only animals, birds singing, little animals chirping, and squirrels and chipmunks and rabbits.
quotes.speaker: Pamela Nance

quotes.text: I could see children, adults, cats, dogs, birds, butterflies, lots of butterflies, and every kind of animal playing and singing in the meadow.
they keep them in these beautiful meadows where they play with each other
Feeding on the green, green grass were fat and happy horses, and animals of all kinds were scattered all over the green hills
quotes.speaker: David Sunfellow

quotes.text: there was a swan off in the distance who didn't speak to me in a normal vocal sense, but it was more in a way of telepathy
quotes.speaker: Scott Drummond

places.notes: Tagged 'being' rather than 'landscape' because these are encountered as persons, not scenery — but they belong here because they are almost always met IN the meadow or the hills rather than anywhere else. Nearly doubles from 3.68% (all) to 6.77% (cv>=18) before dropping at cv>=23 on 181 docs. Precision ~0.6; the residual false positives are earthly pets in the biographical setup and post-NDE animal-communication aftereffects. Audit found false positives of the form: Post-NDE aftereffect passages: 'now the birds sing more vividly to me', playing with butterflies/cats back on earth (4 passages); Ordinary-life birds: birds on the way to the hospital, birds singing on a spring drive, ravens on a real mountain during an OBE over the physical world; Metaphor and commentary: Plato using 'birds flying' as an analogy for out-of-body travel; Eben-Alexander-style philosophy about 'the trees, the birds, the sky' as an internal construct; Passages with no animal at all that matched on garden/paradise vocabulary (flowers filling a room; a waterfall of stars; 'lint particles').

places.name: The Air and the Scent
places.description: Smell is one of the least expected but most insistently reported senses in this landscape. The air is described as sweet, crisp, clean, pure — 'crystal clear' even to look at — and carrying a floral fragrance with no earthly equivalent. Some name specific flowers (roses, jasmine, gardenia, lilies, freesia); several say the scent returns to them years later on earth and takes them straight back.
sensory: sweet, crisp, clean, pure — never heavy or cloying
floral: roses, jasmine, gardenia, tuberose, lilies, freesia
air that looks crystal clear, not just smells clean
a gentle warm breeze on the skin, or air 'moving yet still'
the grass itself carrying a smell and a taste
the scent recognised again years later on earth

quotes.text: The air was pure and clean, crisp and sweet. It was filled with the fragrance of wildflowers that danced in the warm silken breeze that touched my skin.
quotes.speaker: Sharon

quotes.text: I noticed that I could feel the grass on my feet and it was soft. And I could, the air was sweet and crisp.
quotes.speaker: Sharon Milliman

quotes.text: A clear water stream was flowing, and there was sweet smell to the air.
quotes.speaker: Rajiv Parti

quotes.text: the smell is just heavenly flowers. Then you can never the beautiful, sweetest smelling fragrance.
quotes.speaker: Leslie Fleman

quotes.text: there's a scent to heaven and it's the scent of the most beautiful roses that you could imagine
quotes.speaker: Raymond O'Brien

places.notes: Nearly doubles from all accounts (1.78%) to cv>=18 (3.31%) before dropping back at cv>=23 on a small denominator. The main false-positive source is post-NDE aftereffect passages in which returnees describe smelling earthly flowers with new intensity, and one recurring scriptural phrase ('a sweet smelling savour'). Audit found false positives of the form: 'The air was filled with smiles, songs, and the sweet voices of these little souls' — air as a carrier of sound, no scent and no quality of air (E2srnfBuOJM).; Host reading someone else's written account and joking about whether heaven smells of gasoline (gvKOCuaOWV4).; One passage where the flower smell belongs to the return-to-earth sequence (being called to dinner, tantrums about her name) rather than the other world (m8lqk4fS4cA)..

places.name: The Gate
places.description: The entrance structure to the city or to heaven, and the point at which the question of whether you may enter is decided. Some see many gates of which only one is open; some see a narrow gate beside a wide one; some are set down just inside it. A recurring reinterpretation: the gate is not a barrier keeping people out but an energetic threshold that cleanses whoever passes through. A large minority mention gates specifically to say they expected them and did not find any.

aliases.note: far more often invoked as an expectation than as something seen
Revelation-framed; eleven closed, one open
explicitly not a fence - a cleansing threshold
used when the shape has no hinges or bars

aliases.term: a large black gate with vertical bars

sensory: gates described as simply massive, out of scale with anything earthly
a multi-coloured archway with colours the speaker cannot name
only one gate open among many closed ones
a welcoming committee standing at the gate
the gate as the exact point past which there is no coming back
mother-of-pearl surface, 'white pearl with these blue streaks in it'
a gate of many brilliant colours the experiencer had no names for
standing open with dishes clanging and music audible beyond

quotes.text: There was a gate. One side of the gate was open, and on the other, the gate was gold. And on the other side of the gate, everything was gold.
quotes.speaker: Christa Marie

quotes.text: I saw a huge crowd of people standing in front of the Gates of Heaven.
quotes.speaker: Jeff

quotes.text: And then there was these huge gates. They were massive.
quotes.speaker: Anne Murphy

quotes.text: the only one open is a narrow door and a narrow gate that in front of me
quotes.speaker: Santosh

quotes.text: there was a city behind her, and there were these gates to the city
quotes.speaker: Phill Urena

places.notes: The gate is the most culturally pre-loaded structure in the region, and its frequency DROPS at the highest cvNDE stratum (5.25% at cv>=13 down to 3.31% at cv>=23) - the opposite of the city and the columned hall. That is a meaningful negative signal worth preserving. Audit found false positives of the form: 'pearly gates' invoked as cultural belief rather than perception — 'if you take your own life you're not allowed into the pearly gates', 'if you believe you'll see Pearly Gates you will manifest Pearly Gates', 'I didn't necessarily believe in the pearly gates' (bnZ2KyfwAuw, BXtPCN_At9Q, Fk7V4k3p3Ms); gate as pure metaphor — people with 'a gate down' hiding their light, joy as 'the gateway to the connections', God 'opened the gate and said, go be happy' (0HGnO-tzeqw, M9uYYdU4j6w, 3woD7R1upDU); ordinary earthly gates — opening the garden gate for arriving guests, dogs shut behind a gate at home (ySsEry7ozj0, V1JQfgpoHUg); doctrine recalled, not seen — 'Jesus died to open the gates of heaven for all mankind'; scripture polemic about 'locking up the gate to heaven' (Vrnilxu3Wq8, A9WK6I6m-Tc); gates seen in a dream or a prayer vision rather than in an NDE (amZKVHDf8Kc, IKrq_fUG97M, zcSGNnlzAdo); a place name — locals call Black Rock Beach 'the gateway to the spirit world' (o5ouL9BVUDs); a gate of hell, a different place sharing the word (4_xBUvfnbyc).

places.name: Looking Back at the Earth
places.description: A distinct waypoint reported by people who keep going up: the planet is seen whole and from outside, curved, shrinking, spinning, with land masses recognisable, and then space itself - stars, planets, galaxies moving past. Some describe it matter-of-factly as looking like NASA footage, which they had not seen before their experience.

aliases.term: seeing the planet from the outside
the earth getting smaller / going away
among the stars / the star-forming region

sensory: land masses recognisable as the planet recedes
silence out there, despite the movement
stars that turn out to be moving, or to be other beings
sometimes reached through a doorway rather than by flying

quotes.text: My spirit was traveling very fast, and I saw the Earth below me, and I seemed to be amidst the stars.
quotes.speaker: Anne

quotes.text: I can see the curvature of the earth and everything as I go out.
quotes.speaker: Wayne Fowler

quotes.text: And I remember going into outer space, and it was really fast.
quotes.speaker: Dean Braxton

quotes.text: I was up above the earth, and I could see the earth spinning around real fast.
quotes.speaker: Victor Hicks

quotes.text: settling on the threshold of a doorway that looked into outer space. Pieces of rock floated by, and in the distance, planets and galaxies spun and whirled.
quotes.speaker: Sarah

places.notes: LESS common among the best-evidenced accounts: 3.16% overall, falling to 1.66% at cvNDE>=23 - the opposite direction from the waiting room, which is worth noting since both are OBE-phase perceptions but only one is checkable. Not represented in the catalogued map, which stops at the roof. Audit found false positives of the form: Dominant junk: the idiom 'out into the universe' / 'into outer space' used figuratively — thoughts going out into the universe, 'kick the word should out into outer space', signs that 'go out into the universe', souls who will 'go out into the universe and do good', meditation to 'get out into the universe at large'. Six passages, all of them pure figure of speech; Commentary about NASA spacecraft and planetary frequencies; Trance-journey and dream travel to space that the speaker frames as neither an NDE nor an OBE; Passages where 'space' is only the setting of the life review (bubbles of lifetimes) with no planet, stars or recession described.

places.name: The Light Speaks
places.description: Communication out of the light, almost always without sound. People report the light saying things — 'you can come in', 'it's not your time', 'welcome home' — while insisting the words were not heard with ears and that no language was used. The corpus's own repeated formula is that meaning arrived whole and was translated afterwards into words. In the corpus's entity census, telepathy (2,942 encounters) rivals verbal communication (3,900).

aliases.term: a voice came from the light
it emanated to me in a telepathic way
an amorphous intelligence said to me without language

sensory: heard 'in my head', not with the ears, often with no sense of a mouth or direction
concepts arrive whole and are 'translated' into sentences afterwards
sometimes a single booming voice, sometimes a chorus of many lights in unison
recurring utterances: 'if you want, come on in', 'it's not your time', 'welcome home, [name]'

quotes.text: And as I moved to the edge of the river, the light spoke. The light itself spoke and said, 'It is not time.'
quotes.speaker: Reinee Pasarow

quotes.text: It was as if the light said
quotes.speaker: Halessa

quotes.text: And then the light spoke to me
the light emanated to me in a telepathic way
quotes.speaker: Tom

places.notes: MORE common among better-evidenced accounts (2.01% all, 2.62% at cv>=18, 2.76% at cv>=23). Lower precision because the 'communicat*' arm catches communication from other beings standing in the light rather than from the light itself — a distinction the experiencers themselves often decline to make. Audit found false positives of the form: Relayed accounts of someone else's NDE: a son quoting his father's ('the light said, Earl, you have to go back') and a researcher recounting a rabbi's void experience.; Metaphor: 'the light speaks for itself, you know it when you feel it' in a talk about sharing NDEs.; A telepathic being at the tunnel border rather than the light itself - on-corpus for telepathy, off-claim for 'the light speaks'.; Note: at least six true positives are the same 'you must return, you have a purpose' account retold across different channels; treat the underlying account count as much lower than the match count..

places.name: The Light That Is Alive
places.description: For a substantial minority the light is not illumination but a person. They report recognising, usually in a single instant and without being told, that the light is aware, that it is looking back at them, that it has 'a life to it all by itself'. Several describe the same discovery in near-identical words: 'the light was alive. It was living love.' This is the hinge on which the Light stops being a place and becomes an Other.

aliases.term: it wasn't just a light; it was a presence

sensory: the light 'looks back' — in every direction it returns your gaze with recognition
pulsating, vibrating, humming with energy
palpable — you can feel it on you, not just see it
expands INTO you, filling every cell

quotes.text: I discovered that the glowing golden globe of light was alive. It was a self. It was a living, aware, loving being.
quotes.speaker: D.S Weiler

quotes.text: I recognize that the light is alive. It has a life to it all by itself.
quotes.speaker: Wayne Fowler

quotes.text: There was this unbelievable, exciting, and enlightening living light. It was loving, it was kind and warm
quotes.speaker: Kanan KAS

places.notes: Roughly flat across strata (1.78% all, 1.66% at cv>=18, 2.21% at cv>=23) — the tighter phrasing costs recall badly; a looser regex on 'alive' near 'light' hits 9.25% but drops to ~40% precision because 'everything was alive' describes the landscape, not the Light. Audit found false positives of the form: Light that is a person in a different sense — individual souls seen as balls/tangles of light (JXj-XeY8HB4), or 'the light in everything that was alive' where the light is in living things rather than being the living Other (DbqQ2EP93yI).; Channel and book material: an artist's painting of 'the living light that was God' plus a plug for Heaven Is for Real (ub4fkjcV6Bo); taxonomy talk about categories of NDE with no encounter (BXtPCN_At9Q, 8NRb1MdnmJ4).; 'Realm of living light' used as scene-setting for a pre-birth experience rather than an aware light looking back (Mo2dBMci8OM)..

places.name: The Rushing Sound
places.description: The crossing is loud. People report a whoosh, a roar like rushing wind or a waterfall, a buzz like a flatlined heart monitor, humming, whirring 'almost like vast machinery', a jet-engine noise rising in the ears, or a wind-speed hiss as they are shot forward. The sound usually arrives at the moment of separation or during the passage and stops on arrival, often replaced by music or by absolute silence. Several describe it as unpleasant or alarming at the time and only benign in retrospect.

aliases.note: 'a loud buzz like the heart monitor sound when it goes flat'
'a roaring sound like rushing wind'
'sounds of humming and buzzing and whirring, almost like vast machinery'
occasionally read as Pentecost imagery
often replaces the noise halfway down the passage

sensory: located in the ears or throughout the whole body
rising in volume before separation, cutting off on arrival
compared to machinery, a jet engine, a waterfall, a freight train, a flatline tone
streaked light that can be heard as well as seen — a Doppler-like passing sound
melodies replacing the noise partway along the passage
sudden total silence as the alternative outcome

quotes.text: I "heard" a loud buzzing sound and also a "rushing" sound, like Niagara Falls. Suddenly, I found myself outside my body and beside my bed
all of a sudden, I heard this loud sort of rushing or whooshing sound
quotes.speaker: Dr. Yvonne Kason

quotes.text: There's a sudden stirring and a roaring sound like rushing wind, and I swirl around in a descending spiral, zooming downward at great speed.
quotes.speaker: Bettina Peyton

quotes.text: It made a loud whooshing, whirring sound, similar to my sleep paralysis sound but slightly different.
quotes.speaker: Nannci

quotes.text: No heartbeat, just a loud buzz like the heart monitor sound when it goes flat.

places.notes: MORE common among well-evidenced accounts up to cv>=18 (3.92% all vs 5.66%), falling back at cv>=23 (4.42%, n=8 — small). Precision is the weakest in this region: 'whoosh' is also used for pain, for keys falling in a lake, and for emotional release, and 'vibration/humming' collide with the corpus's pervasive New Age frequency vocabulary. Reported honestly at 0.65. The sound is almost certainly under-counted: many describe it without any of these nouns ('a loud bumpy ride', 'a jolt and then a jolt'). Audit found false positives of the form: Physical-world noise at the moment of injury: the sound of the car crash, the noise of a sandstorm; Sounds heard INSIDE the destination rather than during the crossing — humming from trees, light beams that buzz as they pass through the head (two passages), whale-song and wind-chime sounds of other worlds; Generalised instruction about what one 'may hear' during separation — a teaching, not a report; 'whoosh' as a narrative sound effect in biography (an entity stepping in to defend the body); A roaring sound as a lingering post-NDE aftereffect days later, not at the crossing.

places.name: Welcome Home
places.description: The greeting itself, reported as a fixed formula: the beings, the crowd, or a single relative say 'welcome home', often adding 'we've been waiting for you'. It is not merely a greeting to a visitor — it is spoken as a return. Experiencers who had no home in life report this as the most emotionally overwhelming moment of the whole experience.

aliases.note: the exact phrase, frequently in quotation marks in the transcript
the usual second clause
spoken by a meditation teacher's presence in one account

sensory: arrives telepathically as a whole meaning rather than as words
sometimes spoken in an unknown language that is nevertheless understood
delivered by a crowd speaking as one voice
reported by people who grew up in foster care or dysfunctional homes as unbearable in its sweetness

quotes.text: And all of them knew me, and they all said in the giant chorus, 'Welcome home, Andy.' And I said out loud, 'I'm home at last! I'm home!'
quotes.speaker: David Sunfellow

quotes.text: Welcome home. Welcome. We've been waiting for you.
my grandfather is extending his hands to me and saying, "Welcome home, Donnie," in a language I've never heard before, but fully understood.
quotes.speaker: John Burke

quotes.text: Then I heard her speak inside my mind, "Welcome home. You have come home."
quotes.speaker: Bettina Peyton

quotes.text: they communicated to me a thought, a meaning, a perception of welcome home. And I'll tell you, it was the most emotional homecoming I think I could have ever experienced
quotes.speaker: Dave Bennett

places.notes: Distinct from the already-catalogued welcoming-party (who is there) — this entry is what is said. Note the drop at cvNDE>=23 (0.55%, 1 of 181): the very best-evidenced accounts are dominated by short, medically-verified OBEs that never reach the greeting stage, so absence here is a truncation artefact, not disconfirmation. Audit found false positives of the form: Generic speculation about what happens to everyone: 'the moment that we cross over... all those who loved us will be waiting for us singing welcome home'.; Theological framing rather than report: 'God says, thank you, welcome home. Let me love you again' - immediately followed by channel intro boilerplate.; Conditional / future promise rather than the greeting itself: 'you will be loved and welcomed home regardless', 'I can go there and I can be welcomed home'.; One non-NDE mystical vision: voices of the fay saying 'Welcome home, daughter' at a spring, in a pagan otherworld experience rather than a near-death event.; Note: five true positives are the same Archangel Michael formula from what appear to be four re-tellings by one experiencer plus one near-duplicate pair, so the account count behind this node is smaller than the match count suggests..

places.name: the one who watches with you
places.description: Almost nobody reviews their life alone. A presence stands beside, behind or around the experiencer for the duration - a guide, an angel of light, a being of light, Jesus, a soul family, or something unseen that can only be sensed. Its function is remarkably consistent: it does not narrate and does not accuse. It says 'why don't we look at this', it pauses the review to discuss a scene, it holds the experiencer while they weep, and it answers their self-condemnation with love. Where the experiencer expected a prosecutor they found a companion.

aliases.note: in some accounts the whole group relives your life with you
explicitly invisible, sensed only

sensory: standing behind or slightly to one side, often unseen
communicating without speech; questions rather than statements
pausing the review to ask 'okay, how do you feel about that?'
physical holding - arms around you while the worst scenes run

quotes.text: And the other one stood in front of me, beside me, as we watched my life review.
quotes.speaker: Jeff Cleckley

quotes.text: during the time that I was being shown this review of my life, he was with me in all of it.
quotes.speaker: Vicky Noratuk

quotes.text: And then I realize right at the end, that there is a presence next to me. I can't see him, I know he's male, and I know that I know him intimately.
quotes.speaker: Angie Fenimore

quotes.text: There was something loving beside me. It wasn’t anything visible. You could only sense it. It was a kind of spirit or soul.

places.notes: The strongest cvNDE gradient anywhere in this region: 2.23% of all accounts but 6.63% of the best-evidenced ones, a threefold enrichment. Whatever else the review is, the presence of a non-judging companion is disproportionately reported by the accounts with the strongest veridical corroboration. Recall is limited because many describe the companion without any of these anchor phrases. Audit found false positives of the form: Bare 'life review' with no companion of any kind in the passage (3 passages) - the regex appears to fire on the review, not on the presence.; Explicit negation: 'There was no, of some spiritual being standing with me as I watched my life unfold on a screen. It was none of that.'; Contradicts the claim's ordering: one speaker's review glimpse happened before he met his guide ('It was essentially right before'), i.e. he reviewed alone.; Someone else's review: the speaker sits in an audience watching another man's life review on a stage.; Self-only review with no other presence: the theatre account where director, producer, actor and scriptwriter are all the experiencer..

places.name: Passing Up Through the Ceiling and the Roof
places.description: The ceiling stops being a barrier. People report being drawn or shot straight up through the ceiling of the room, then through the floors above, then through the roof, and out into the open air — sometimes narrating the building shrinking beneath them. Solid matter offers no resistance; several remark with surprise that it did not hurt. This is often the immediate step between the ceiling vantage and the tunnel or the sky.

aliases.term: pulled up through the ceiling of this floor up through another floor
sucked through the ceiling like a vacuum
floated straight up through the ceiling, face first

aliases.note: the downward inversion of the same move

sensory: no resistance, no pain — surprise that solid matter does not stop you
floor-by-floor ascent through a hospital building
the building, cars and streets shrinking below
sometimes 'face first' orientation
occasionally the reverse on return: coming back down through the roof of the vehicle

quotes.text: So I moved up through the ceiling and I saw in the ceiling all the suitcases and the boxes, and I thought, "Wow, this is very cool."
quotes.speaker: Philippe Roels

quotes.text: We floated straight up through the ceiling, face first.
And I was pulled through the roof of the dentist office up into the sky, up into this tunnel.
quotes.speaker: Philip Syracusa

quotes.text: I just felt my soul rising up through the ceiling into the atmosphere.
quotes.speaker: Mindy Speranza

quotes.text: I floated up through the through the ceiling, through the roof of the house.
quotes.speaker: Kevin Jeffers

places.notes: MUCH more common among the best-evidenced accounts: 2.04% overall rising to 7.73% at cv>=23, a 3.8x enrichment — the steepest gradient of any item in this region. Likely for the same reason as the ceiling vantage: accounts detailed enough to describe the exit route are also detailed enough to score on veridical criteria. The unconstrained phrase 'through the ceiling/roof/wall/window' hits 9.99% but is heavily contaminated by literal windows and the idiom 'went through the roof'. Audit found false positives of the form: The idiom 'went through the roof': 'My energy went through the roof' after cutting out meat (Sq1NhW9mwxw).; A white light leaving through the car ceiling rather than the person passing through it — the same story from one experiencer on two channels (a3ahyF00aaw, j5wd-MufFy0).; Interviewer summarising and the experiencer contradicting him: 'You don't remember going through the roof of the hospital... It's just that, by magic, you were already outside the planet' (1AqyxjuZ_go).; Judgment call worth flagging: I counted three passages where the ceiling/roof is passed downward on the way back (JHzBNw0evfI, fRcFquC46bk, 8ePE5EBbkhI). They are the same permeability phenomenon but reverse the direction the claim asserts; if the map insists on 'up', precision drops to 0.708..

places.name: Rising — Going Up Without a Tunnel
places.description: For a large minority there is no passage at all, only lift. They rise: above the body, above the trees, above the accident, above the hospital, up into the sky and then into a starfield, watching the world recede. The motion is sometimes gentle drift and sometimes rocket-like — 'insane G's' — but it is always upward and always without walls. Several describe an 'up and over' arc rather than a straight climb.

aliases.term: going up and up and up
climbing up in this blue sky

sensory: the ground, cars and buildings shrinking with changing perspective
'insane G's' in the fast version; effortless drift in the slow one
an 'up and over' curve rather than a straight vertical
darkness and a starfield opening above
the Earth becoming visible below

quotes.text: Slowly I floated upward, out of the room and building, above the trees, and up into a black, star-filled sky.
I shot up into the sky.
quotes.speaker: Louisa Peck

quotes.text: I shot up straight into the air, like straight up towards, uh, the sky.
soon I realized that I was floating up above the earth, and it was dark
quotes.speaker: Kenneth Leth

quotes.text: here was still rising up through the air and the cars, the vehicles were getting smaller
quotes.speaker: Brad Barrows

places.notes: Modestly MORE common in strongly-evidenced accounts (3.25% all vs 4.83% cv>=18, 4.42% cv>=23). This is the main alternative to the tunnel for the outbound leg and often replaces it entirely: several who deny a tunnel describe exactly this instead. The measured figure is a floor, not a ceiling — much rising is described with verbs too generic to isolate safely. Audit found false positives of the form: Dominant junk: plain out-of-body ceiling hovering ('I floated up to the corner of the ceiling and looked down at my body') — 7 passages. That is the leaving-the-body feature, which has its own packet; it is not the ascent past the room into sky and starfield that this claim describes; Secondhand narration of someone else's rise (a host recounting Robert's drowning, a daughter quoting her father, a third-person retelling of a woman floating up a stairway); A nitrous-oxide float out of a dentist's chair and a meditative OBE — lift, but not during a near-death event; Hovering with no upward motion (suspended 20 feet over a desert scene); One passage where the lift is immediately followed by entering a cylinder/tunnel, which contradicts the 'without a tunnel' qualifier the claim rests on.

places.name: inside the other person
places.description: The signature detail of the whole region: during the review you do not merely watch what you did, you experience it from the position of the person you did it to. Experiencers say they were inside the other person's body, brain and emotions, feeling the exact hurt or comfort they had caused, often simultaneously with their own original justification for causing it. Several describe consciousness fragmenting into multiple streams so that one event is lived from every participant's side at once. This is the mechanic that turns the review from information into moral experience - and it is the reason many say a bad review is what hell actually means.

aliases.term: from the other person's point of view
through their eyes / through everyone's perspective
the golden rule written into the fabric of the universe

sensory: being inside the other person's body, brain and physical suffering
your own justification running simultaneously alongside their pain
the pain you gave described as disproportionate in size - 'the size of a mountain'
the good is felt the same way: you receive the gratitude of people you helped
seeing how the person then carried the hurt onward into other lives

quotes.text: all the pain that I gave to them, because I experienced it from their point of view, as if I was them, juxtaposed to all of my reasons for causing their pain simultaneously.
quotes.speaker: Peter Panagore

quotes.text: I also was able to feel as though I was the other person that I was interacting with. And if I had behaved hurtfully, I was feeling that hurt of that other person.
quotes.speaker: Karen Thomas

quotes.text: I felt what they felt, juxtaposed and simultaneous to my own justifications and emotional state for causing them their, my reasons, my hurt.
quotes.speaker: Peter Panagore

quotes.text: you relive it from the perspective of everyone involved. So if you've been busy handing out pain and suffering to others in your life review, you'll be on the receiving end of that.
quotes.speaker: Vinnie Todd Tolman

places.notes: Almost certainly under-counted: many describe the mechanic without any of these fixed phrases ('I was in that person as they experience it'). The wording is highly idiosyncratic, so recall is the weak point, not precision. Requiring life-review proximity would raise precision but collapses the count to 47 docs (0.76%), so the looser form is reported. Note this element does NOT rise with cvNDE - it is slightly less common in the best-evidenced accounts, unlike most of this region. Audit found false positives of the form: Third-person explanations of the phenomenon rather than reports of it — a narrator on dying-brain theory ('people usually describe... they experience it from the perspective of everybody else'), and one experiencer who explicitly disclaims ('I'm probably not the best one to describe these life reviews because I was so young'); 'See through the other person's eyes' used as moral advice for this life ('why do we have to wait until it's too late?'); Ordinary-life 'I was that person' (a recovering alcoholic identifying with newcomers); Perspective shifts that are not the injured party's: seeing one's life through God's eyes, merging with a squirrel, inhabiting a past-life self; A novelist describing writing her book 'through his eyes'.

places.name: The Sky Without a Sun
places.description: The sky over the country is usually blue — often a deeper, richer blue than earth's, sometimes with clouds — but there is no sun in it, and nothing casts a shadow. Experiencers frequently notice this only when they try to orient themselves, and then realise the light is not falling on things from outside but coming out of them. A pilot who tried to find the sun to work out his compass direction is the clearest example.

aliases.note: often quoted alongside Isaiah/Revelation

aliases.term: a darker blue sky than we're used to

aliases.note: reported in several Portuguese-language accounts

sensory: blue, deeper and more saturated than any earthly blue
bright as a sunny day with nothing overhead producing it
no shadows under leaves, rocks, people, or oneself
light that never hurts the eyes however bright
warmth without heat

quotes.text: the sky was blue. It was like the sun was shining, but there really wasn't a sun in the sky. Everything was lit up.
quotes.speaker: Sharon Milliman

quotes.text: And this beautiful vault of a darker blue sky than we're used to here on Earth, but no sun.
quotes.speaker: Jim Woodford

quotes.text: there was no sun in the sky, but it was all light. But that made sense to me because the light was coming from within every molecule
quotes.speaker: Michelle Clare

quotes.text: There were no shadows. The leaves, there were no shadows under the leaves, the rocks.
There was no external source of light like our sun. There wasn't that. The light was coming from inside.
quotes.speaker: Vinney Tolman

places.notes: A small but very consistent detail, and one people frequently volunteer as evidence against hallucination because it surprised them. False positives come from the dark void ('no stars, no sun, no moon' describes the darkness, not the country) and from one aftereffect discussion of sungazing. Prevalence is flat across strata rather than enriched. Audit found false positives of the form: The dark realm's sunlessness, which is a different place sharing the words: black leafless trees where 'there was no sunlight, you couldn't tell if it was night or day', and a dark void with 'no sun and moon and all that stuff' (2 passages, one of which also carries a sponsor read).; The void described as a list of absences ('no colour, no movement, no form, no texture, no sun') - not a sky at all.; Discussion of the earthly sun as our spiritual home (Kundalini talk), and a Revelation 21 exegesis by a host summarising what blind experiencers report.; An ambiguous aside, 'for me, there was no sunshine in my story', which is a comment about the account's mood rather than a sky.; Caveat for the map: 3 of the 18 true positives (2 speakers) describe the shadowless, self-luminous light during an out-of-body episode in an earthly bedroom or street, not the sky over the country. They belong to 'lit from within' more than to 'the sky'..

places.name: The nothingness / annihilation
places.description: Not darkness with something in it, but the absence of anything at all — including the self.
