places.notes: LESS common among better-evidenced accounts (1.26% all vs 1.10% at cv>=18 and cv>=23; only 0.78% at cv>=13). Genuinely rare. The corpus is overwhelmingly Anglophone-Christian in composition, so this is a sampling fact about the corpus at least as much as about the afterlife. About a third of matches are commentary about other people's experiences rather than the speaker's own. Audit found false positives of the form: Comparative-religion talk rather than a naming: 'if I was a Buddhist, I would call the light Buddha. If I was a Hindu, it would be Krishna' (two near-duplicate passages), 'one person will say I saw Buddha, the other will say I saw Krishna'; Second-hand reports: 'some saw Buddha, some saw Jesus', a Burmese monk who saw the Buddha in hell (with book plug), a researcher's summary; The historical Buddha as an example in teaching ('Buddha reached the Buddhahood enlightenment'), or as a quoted authority; Names attached to other kinds of experience: a psychedelic session where 'the Happy Buddha appeared in the grass', mystical journeys 'into the mind of Buddha', Brahman/Parabrahman practice phases; Objects and similes: a Buddha statue in an aunt's house, 'it was like I was a little Buddha sitting there on the bed'.

places.name: The Web of Light
places.description: A minority but strikingly consistent image: the fabric of the place is visible as a mesh - a spiderweb, matrix or lattice of light with everything strung on it, and the experiencer embedded inside it rather than looking at it. The lights in the web are alive. Some see the same structure while still at the ceiling, as threads running out of the heads of the living.

aliases.note: recurs almost verbatim across unrelated accounts
seen attached to living people

sensory: woven, intricate, streaming in every direction
you are inside it, not observing it
the lights in the mesh are alive
initially mistaken for constellations

quotes.text: I started moving into what I would describe as a spiderweb of light, just a beautiful matrix of light that was just streaming everywhere, and I was embedded in it.
quotes.speaker: Deborah King

quotes.text: what appeared to be almost a very intricately woven spiderweb of light, it's the only way I can describe it
quotes.speaker: Dianne Sherman

quotes.text: Vivid rays of light, and what appeared to be almost a very intricately woven spiderweb of light.
quotes.speaker: Deborah King

places.notes: Rare - 29 documents - and the strata are too thin to read a gradient (0.47% overall, 1.10% at cv>=23 on n=181). Reported here because it is entirely absent from the catalogued map and because the phrasing 'spiderweb of light' recurs near-verbatim in unrelated accounts, which is the signature of a shared percept rather than a shared metaphor. Broadening to include 'beams of light' triples the count but captures beings, not structure. Audit found false positives of the form: Dominant junk: 'web of light' as a post-NDE metaphor for the community of awakened people - 'we are part of this web of light living on the earth', 'the worldwide web of light grows stronger', 'I do feel that we are a web' (docs Q_zxxxlz-BY, erdr_f7Q3Lo, -rbvd7s4o1A). Five of nine FPs are this.; New Age cosmology being taught rather than perceived: 'the good matrix, the universal consciousness, the web of energy', 'the grid of light that exists on the planet' (docs WMpe7PNqgZ0, 3YMv3-FTVkI).; Ayahuasca-ceremony teaching about 'the matrix we're in', which appears twice from the same speaker (docs wh5DaS6zyww, zwqIXOFCQTc).; Post-NDE psychic impressions of trees as 'a network of energy' (doc kiHW1mmCoB0)..

places.name: The Nursery
places.description: A building, or an area with a large green space around it, where infants are. Speakers are told - usually because they ask what that beautiful building is - that this is where babies who died before or at birth, including the unborn, are raised and taught until they understand. There are attendants: angels, family members, people specifically trained for it. Children are seen running, playing and growing there, and some describe wanting to come back after death to work in it.

aliases.note: the word given to the experiencer by a guide, not chosen by them

aliases.term: an area where the babies and the unborn fetuses are brought
a place where souls were born and nurtured and grown
aliases.note: pre-birth framing rather than post-death
one speaker's term for Earth itself, by analogy

thousands of children playing outside with birds, dogs and cats

places.notes: Doubles in prevalence between the whole corpus and the cv>=18 stratum (1.23% -> 2.35%). Remaining precision loss after the lookarounds is hospital nurseries recalled from infancy and earthly childcare biography. Note the split between the post-death nursery (children who died) and the pre-birth nursery (souls not yet incarnated) - same building, opposite direction of travel. Audit found false positives of the form: hospital newborn/neonatal nursery - the medical setting, not the other world (5 passages); daycare 'nursery' the speaker drops a child at, church nursery, Crisis Nursery charity; astronomical 'star nursery' / stellar nursery seen in space, and 'larval nursery' as a metaphor for Earth; plant nursery on an organic farm; a YouTube channel handle ('encrypted angels nursery') read out as boilerplate; a planned earthly community building that 'will have a nursery'.

places.name: It Wasn't a Place
places.description: The rarest and most philosophically explicit form: narrators who reject the whole category of location. They report an environment, an atmosphere, a condition — but insist it had no buildings, no landscape, no geography as we mean it. One describes becoming uncomfortable precisely BECAUSE it was not a place, wishing it looked more like one, whereupon a landscape appeared as if painted in. That account is the corpus's sharpest single hint about how the scenery in these experiences may be generated.
sensory: presence without extension
no colours or dimension until wanted
scenery arriving after the wish for scenery
an atmosphere with no container

quotes.text: And then I started to feel uncomfortable because it wasn't a place. And we're used to colors and then 3D and dimension. And I thought, "I wish it looked more like a place."
quotes.speaker: Ellyn Dye

quotes.text: But it wasn't a place like here. It was an environment, an atmosphere. And it was love.
quotes.speaker: Ellyn

quotes.text: This wasn't a physical place with buildings and landscapes as we understand them.
quotes.speaker: Vinney Todd Tolman

places.notes: Very rare in absolute terms (35 docs) but monotonically enriched with evidential strength (0.57% -> 1.10% at cv>=23), nearly a doubling. False positives include 'it wasn't a placebo' and 'there wasn't a place to really help people', both handled by the negative_regex. Worth flagging for follow-up: the Ellyn Dye account (NyfUJD1xf08 / NXKFo5lJUjA, the same experiencer under two uploads) describes the landscape being generated on demand, which if it recurs elsewhere would be a significant structural finding about the whole otherworld map. Audit found false positives of the form: 'Not a place OF X' constructions, which are evaluations rather than denials of location: 'it wasn't a place of punishment', 'it was not a place of sadness', 'it wasn't a place of passage', 'it was not a place where you would want to be' (docs CcRIwKX2QaM, hMSWWKrTeEA, o4JcqQPaoVo, B3yfVunO1t0).; Interviewer framing rather than experiencer testimony - two packets are the same host's question 'gives the impression that it was not a material place' (docs En-uQwoKdRA, ruQIUNs-xYs, O1f0heJGsUM).; The exact OPPOSITE claim: 'I've heard people say that heaven isn't a physical place, and I disagree... I think it is an actual place' (doc vko4tnKFRA8).; General theology about where souls go, not a perceived environment (doc Ht8fFjCAYNA), and plain ordinary-life idiom - Babaji's cave 'wasn't a place you could tour to', 'there wasn't a place to really help people' (docs IGj-rUp7sD0, 5U5VhcILuxk)..

places.name: the line on the ground
places.description: The barest possible object: a line. Sometimes visible — a yellow line of light on the floor, a black zig-zag across a tan wall — and sometimes explicitly invisible or imaginary, a line the experiencer knows is 'over there to my right' without seeing anything. Crossing it, or even saying out loud that one wants to stay, is understood to constitute the crossing.

aliases.note: one account fuses line and threshold
spoken by Jesus in two accounts

sensory: a thick black zig-zag running across a tan-coloured wall
a yellow line 'made of light' on the floor by a door
known to be 'off to my right, I don't know how many feet away' while unseen

quotes.text: I saw ... a line on the floor by the door ... like a yellow line ... made of light. But it was a yellow line ... like one ... a divider ... I don't know ... a line that I couldn't cross
quotes.speaker: Mauro Reis Guedes

quotes.text: Further to my left was a tan-colored wall with a thick, black, zig-zag line, all the way across it.
quotes.speaker: Charlyn

quotes.speaker: Donna Rebadow

quotes.text: I understood without being told that if I crossed that line or passed through it, there would be no coming back.
quotes.speaker: Cherylyn

places.notes: Genuinely rare (15 docs) once the biographical 'line in the sand' and 'crossing a line' idioms are excluded — which is worth reporting honestly, because 'a line you must not cross' is the culturally expected image and the corpus does NOT strongly support it. Two of the 15 are the same account told twice (9oNvs75DDEk / vjt-VgrOn7E, 'Charlyn'/'Cherylyn'), so the true document count is lower still. Audit found false positives of the form: 'Crossing a line' as a life metaphor: bereavement ('this line has been crossed in your life... that person's gone') and a self-protective rule adopted after an assault (docs I4PHMgUuTns, 3rAYA_P1pXQ).; A literal geographic line in the ordinary world - reindeer still refusing to cross the old Berlin Wall boundary (doc FNUtgGdfYws).; Note the packet is small and duplicated: 14 matches are about 10 distinct accounts (docs kfmkyqG6oO4/Cpc4xLUfza0, vjt-VgrOn7E/9oNvs75DDEk, c7PK7WmSDhM/TTDNl010QuA are pairs)..

places.name: the golden wall around the city
places.description: A wall that marks where the realm proper begins — most often described as enormous blocks of pure gold, sometimes stone, marble or jasper. Experiencers stand outside it and try, absurdly and unsuccessfully, to jump or climb it; several later realise the gates a few feet along were standing wide open. The wall is repeatedly described as a marker rather than a defence: 'it seemed too low for protection. It just marked the boundary.'

aliases.term: a low wall of glowing golden rocks

sensory: huge cinder-block-sized bricks of solid gold, stacked
so tall it cannot be jumped, yet the gates beside it stand open
sound carries over it — dishes clanging, music, people laughing
in one account it is low, made of glowing golden rocks, with a single gap for a gate

quotes.text: I'm standing at the golden wall that surrounded the Glorious City. And this wall was like real thick, pure gold cinder blocks, and it was so tall. I kept trying to jump the wall
quotes.speaker: Sharon Millerman

quotes.text: I was standing outside of this great big huge golden wall. It was like cinder blocks, one on top of the other, huge ones.
quotes.speaker: Sharon Milliman

quotes.text: there's the golden wall that surrounds the city, which I took to mean that they're, that's the barrier. I couldn't go past that barrier. And if I did, then I wouldn't be coming back.
quotes.speaker: Sharon Milliman

quotes.text: I think the rock wall was the boundary, you know? If I had touched that wall, I don't think I would have came back.
quotes.speaker: Jerry Rogers

quotes.text: And then over that wall on the other side there, I could see these little rolling hills.
quotes.speaker: Betty Cone

places.notes: Rare in absolute terms but strongly skewed toward well-evidenced accounts: 0.36% overall rises to 1.10% at cv>=18 and 1.66% at cv>=23, a 4.6x enrichment — the steepest positive gradient of any object in this region. Caution: Sharon Milliman/Millerman accounts for several of the 22 documents across repeat interviews. Audit found false positives of the form: Other walls in other settings: the white walls of the oval-table review room, seen twice from the same experiencer (docs lMEQ4Oe18FU, aSNVGewTc0M), a low stone wall around a well in a hellish crowd (doc mPWwxnYiq9A), and a white bedroom wall in an optical-illusion experiment at home (doc K9vI9ZTn9fA).; Walls inside the realm that are not the boundary wall: stone walls around houses in an ancient village, and a garden wall with doors leading to life-review scenes (docs 46a6x_wZq70, rfTxpUTdJkc).; MAJOR CAVEAT for the map: 15 of the 16 true positives are one recurring 'Glorious City' testimony re-uploaded across many channels (cMBRXeUtKfs, kfDl0i4Z2sQ, jvhSmwTQ4-E, TsOGyCidXLQ, Bn5Rt-Sx-lE, cbTWrNqyMhM, 9T8RidoORJU, OmmjdXTVWNA, OMr1ntfvwgg, CiTPmS94xfE, 92eTYGTqvOk, b0hqU1UoD0g, Ot_oAFw1Qfw, SKL0T_1vodw, H6KUCZKU8No). Only one independent account (iyl-82q6Ha0, the low wall by the River of Life). The precision is real; the convergence is not..

places.name: the paths not taken
places.description: A rare but vivid extension of the review in which you are shown not only what you did but what you could have done, or what would have followed from a different choice. Some see the alternative words they might have spoken in a given scene; some are shown the life their family would have had without them; one describes being shown his life as a tree whose roots were all the paths that could have led to that moment. Experiencers are consistent that this is not presented to induce guilt but to make the reality of choice visible.

aliases.term: what my life would have been like

aliases.note: one experiencer's image: all the possible paths to the same event

sensory: a tree whose roots are every path that could have reached this moment
a fiber optic cable of many strands, intersecting everywhere
a bedroom fit for princesses - the life the children would have had without her
the alternative sentence you might have spoken, played back
explicitly not framed as accusation

quotes.text: I saw all these paths that I could have taken when I was dead, and in this, it was like looking at the bottom of a large cable, a fiber optic cable made up of many fiber optic cables.
quotes.speaker: Peter Panagore

quotes.text: a lot of times NDErs will say in their life review, they will be shown alternatives of what they could have been and could have said or done.
quotes.speaker: Jeff Janssen

quotes.text: Then I was shown the future without me. It was an apartment and at the end of the hall was a bedroom.
when I died, they showed me my potential. They showed me what I could have been had I lived in alignment with my soul.

places.notes: Genuinely rare - 27 documents - and included because it is vivid and specific rather than common. Two looser regexes were rejected: one including 'alternate realities/timelines' (0.94%) was dominated by parallel-universe speculation, and one including 'what would have happened if' (0.65%) was almost entirely retrospective biographical musing. Even the tightened form mixes shown-during-review alternatives with ordinary regret about roads not taken, hence the modest precision estimate. Zero hits in the cv>=23 stratum, which at n=181 is not evidence of absence. Audit found false positives of the form: 'Things I could have done differently' as ordinary retrospective regret, in this life and after it - business failures, parenting after a child's death, grief counselling, a pastor's 'it's not a path I would have chosen' (docs sL_KGIDJMcI, qmFtC1IHe0E, hdv3lC5mWTU, O_gDiLAN9F0, A2NGV591_Tw, qhYHcNf0sBY, WOcckxpAZeg).; Second-biggest source: one widely re-uploaded life-review account whose 'the things that I could have done and should have done and would have done differently' is regret INSIDE the review, not a display of alternatives (docs 7kDx-wkVzCM, -PNYA4cso1g, FJBZ5rEsJQM).; Generalisations about how life reviews work for everyone, spoken by hosts or teachers (docs 2xskMb26t2M, acbEt8BtJKI, mPc5R8WkwDc).; An OBE overhearing parents argue about 'what they could have done differently' in the waiting room (doc MZpBV3BZ1lc)..

places.name: the hand that stops you
places.description: The boundary enforced by a body. A being puts a hand on the shoulder, an arm across the chest, or simply raises a palm, and forward motion — and often the desire for it — ends instantly. Experiencers stress that there is no force or violence in it; the touch is loving and the pull toward the far side simply disappears at the moment of contact.

aliases.term: he held up his right hand and he goes, 'No'
an arm of a man in a robe stops him
a huge hand gathers up everything about me and stops me

sensory: the weight of a hand felt distinctly on the shoulder
an arm laid across the body from behind
a palm raised with a single silent 'No'
the urge to cross vanishing at the instant of contact

quotes.text: Suddenly, the one standing next to me raised his hand before what I can only equate as my face, stopping me from running forward.
quotes.speaker: Spyro

quotes.text: It was this like an arm, and it held me on my shoulder. And I knew right then and there, I just knew it. It was over. I knew I had to go back.
quotes.speaker: Franco Romero

quotes.text: the lady who was walking with me put her hand on my shoulder from behind. And the second she did, the urge to cross that bridge was gone.
quotes.speaker: Joni Gommo

quotes.text: he starts to go through, walk through the archway into the city when the angel stopped him and and sent him back.
quotes.speaker: Santosh Acci

places.notes: Flat across all cvNDE strata. Precision is limited by the extremely common English idiom 'it stopped me dead in my tracks' used about ordinary life events; the negative_regex removes the most frequent forms. This is the physical-contact variant of the boundary and is the only one where the experiencer's desire to cross is described as being removed rather than overruled. Audit found false positives of the form: Dominant junk (12 of 19 FPs): the phrase 'the being that held me' from a single widely re-uploaded life-review testimony - an EMBRACE during the life review, not a halt. It appears near-verbatim in docs E7OaKzbPWgI, eNETJUp8URI, ZZGPNU28pbo, xiuSeJvsHcQ, lDSDP1tGfJ0, dT_jJEu7kRw, i6KdwZN0f_4, Xna-HGgLytk, z1QtKaNnN8o, ACneU_WZYjg, Z7vnMIgoWe0.; Hospital hands: paramedics putting their hands up to stop a relative reaching the gurney; a charge nurse putting her hand over the narrator's mouth (docs n1kf29odZoU, gpPurcd_ERU).; Ordinary-life scenes and figures of speech: a bridesmaid throwing herself on a car hood with arms out; 'it felt like a hand just held me back from being hit' as an illustration of everyday miracles (docs 8cnODbcgbBg, ZY1h7hqkDnE).; Hands used for something other than stopping - beings placing hands over the ears to relieve pain (doc 5JYUdLF7EAY)..

places.name: The children who were never born
places.description: A small but very consistent cluster: experiencers meet a miscarried, stillborn or aborted child, or a sibling who died as a baby before they were born. The child is not an infant — it is described as a fully developed soul, often aged forward to the years elapsed since the loss, and it initiates the contact ('hi, Mommy'). Separately, many accounts describe children simply playing in the landscape, not as anyone's dead in particular.

aliases.term: the child I never knew on Earth
a little boy / a little girl

sensory: aged forward to match the years since the loss
carried by another dead relative and handed over
named — and the name matches one the family chose but never spoke aloud
children playing at what looks like school recess, with animals among them

quotes.text: Out of the corner of my eye, in a place I should not have been able to see, I saw my sister who died as a baby. Now she was walking down to me and carrying my son.
the little girl says, yes, yes, you are. Uh, you know, I'm, I'm the child you aborted.
quotes.speaker: David Suich

places.notes: Rare but rises monotonically with evidential strength (0.42% -> 1.10%). Some matches are the experiencer's own obstetric history rather than a meeting; I kept the regex tight rather than inflate the count. The broader pattern 'children playing / babies in heaven' matches 226 docs (3.66%) but with much lower specificity, so I did not use it as the measured figure. Audit found false positives of the form: Dominant junk: miscarriage, stillbirth and abortion as BIOGRAPHY - the medical crisis that caused the NDE, or the speaker's obstetric history, with no encounter at all (docs KF1qu6P9pTo, XqtLcCDHSO8, PY5I2sCRQWE, yVxCeJVXGi8, sqaV-SF6pRQ, iAP38LkUxTU, IZBcv4So38s). Seven of eighteen FPs.; Doctrine and speculation about abortion, soul contracts and pre-birth plans, including one anti-NDE-community rant (docs turt5McjUlw, g3yQGY61eFc).; Researchers and hosts summarising the pattern in other people's NDEs - one packet states the entire claim verbatim as a generalisation about 'many NDErs' (docs nWjAa28WEc4, pYjYg1E4I0g).; Interviewer speculation ('what if one of them was the child you aborted?') and prophetic-ministry stories outside any NDE (docs fqQ0xxTmu6o, 7ST8RQYB4EM), plus one prayer-induced heaven visit rather than an NDE (doc mZ5CKy2i5cs)..

places.name: The worms and crawling things
places.description: A rare but startlingly convergent detail: worms, maggots, or insects crawling in, on and through the body, eating flesh that regrows so the eating can continue. Reported by experiencers with no apparent contact with each other and in near-identical terms, including the note that the vermin themselves stink worse than anything else.

aliases.note: Dominic Morrow's coinage: 'thick as soda cans'

aliases.term: things that stick to your body and sear you

sensory: unnatural size — 'thick as soda cans', tarantulas 'ginormous'
an inchworm motion, crawling up the body
entering the body and passing through it
the worst smell in the whole experience comes off them
flesh consumed and restored in a loop

quotes.text: to see them fall inside of a hole and the worms devour their flesh and then then the flesh comes back on over and over again is a sight you just don't forget
quotes.speaker: Bryan W. Melvin

quotes.text: I call them hell maggots because they're thick.
quotes.speaker: Dominic Morrow

quotes.text: they look more like worms, but they just, they would stick to your body and just sear you
quotes.speaker: Joel Brim

places.notes: Genuinely rare — 22 documents in 6,176 — but MORE common in the better-evidenced strata (0.36% -> 0.55% at cv>=18 and cv>=23). I include it precisely because it is rare and specific: three experiencers who share no channel, tradition, or vocabulary independently describe worms that eat flesh which then regrows, and one of them (Bryan Melvin, cv=23) says his publisher asked him to cut it from the book. False positives are earthly phobia talk ('worms crawling all over me, like I was afraid of') rather than experience. Audit found false positives of the form: Simile for trauma, not perception: 'I've had times where I felt like maggots were crawling in my skin' after being raped - appears twice from the same speaker (docs FDyJb9IhFIc, OE2RiW1JmE4).; Ordinary-life religious rhetoric: preachers calling Catholics 'serpents', twice from the same speaker (docs rx1rfPpbI-k, tdRdrfiacns).; Fear-of-the-grave references and an atheist father's mantra 'you're buried, the worms eat you' - explicitly NOT what was experienced (docs WalJw3rI9eo, yu9ljcHcu3w).; Post-NDE aftereffects and dreams about spiders and bugs (docs GJShJRwEf6o, 7cJiP2m6sss), plus 'my reptilian brain' in a hypothermia survival story (doc RVuU5U_0beI).; Adjacent-but-different infernal imagery that does not include vermin in the body: snake-pit past life, demons around pits, spiders on walls, tarantulas laid on bedding (docs M-DWYU1YJMU, gAJShDqxM1E, A2NGV591_Tw, DiqCVc2C9ck)..

places.name: the tree at the top of the hill
places.description: A boundary made of pure desire rather than obstruction: a single tree standing at the crest of a grassy hill, or a distant landmark of the same kind. Nothing bars the way. The experiencer knows that reaching the tree and seeing over the horizon behind it is the crossing, and wants to run to it 'with every fiber of my being'. Being talked out of running is the whole of the boundary.

aliases.term: the other edge of that horizon

sensory: grass so alive that every individual blade is felt as it moves
colours 'more vivid than I've ever experienced here'
light shining through the body from every direction, not from a sun
a single tree, no forest
the tree itself perceived as drinking in the light

quotes.text: And at the top of the hill was that tree. With every fiber of my being, I had to run to that tree
quotes.speaker: David Maginley

quotes.text: There was a tree at the top of the hill, this singular tree.
quotes.speaker: David Maginley

quotes.text: I knew if I got to that tree, I'd never come back here. I was pulled to that tree.
quotes.speaker: David McGinley

quotes.text: I really wanted to go to that tree because I knew if I did, I'd never come back here
quotes.speaker: David Maginley

places.notes: Reported as a genuinely rare vivid specific, with the honest caveat that most of the 12 documents are one experiencer (David Maginley / McGinley) interviewed repeatedly, plus one independent account (ZH0J83t7LZs) where a single beautiful tree stands on the far side of the boundary wall. Zero hits at every cvNDE threshold. Included because the brief asks for rare-but-real detail and because this account articulates the mechanism of a desire-boundary more clearly than any other in the corpus. Audit found false positives of the form: Ordinary-world trees and hills: a car wreck that 'hit a tree' at the top of a hill, and an OBE over a familiar pond where the road 'bent up around the top of the hill' with treetops behind (docs 8X6GcHqiKqk, 8cnODbcgbBg).; Vegetation described as scenery inside the experience but with no single tree and no boundary function - a cerrado-like trail, and walking under trees checking their shadows (docs Cr_Bh4A9lCM, jK_wNH2hxes).; MAJOR CAVEAT for the map: six of the eight true positives are one experiencer (David McGinley) re-interviewed across six channels (AEgxTodIs3o, UPZ5Lat277I, 9uQPuelkQT0, jYXjxZVDWxI, TYiLzS6Jq54, YOi92hxfJgA). Only two independent accounts remain: the tree beyond the rock wall (ZH0J83t7LZs) and the young tree on the hill his boyfriend would 'become' (Q_DrclCSBaU). The image should not be presented as convergent..
